      "observations": [
        "The retained complete eight-path historical source study removes the permissive-import preference and retry prompt, derives permissive mode from !useSecret or !seckey, and adjusts public/secret callers. The fixed source rejects both flags being true; it does not enforce exactly one true flag. Temporary import and permanent import use the same public-versus-secret policy. Current input sanitization and unsupported-feature reporting are later accepted context, not changes credited to this historical patch.",
        "Bug1884337 describes inconsistent message-button and Key Manager import paths. The native secret-key import can report success while importing no keys. The landed code checks JSON key inventory as a separate semantic result and wrappers require importedKeys to be nonempty. Import success, key acceptance and useful encryption/signature capabilities remain different results.",
        "The full human proposal chain matters: proposed original-capability inspection could not work after unsupported packets were stripped. The complex strict-trial/require-both-usages proposal in comment19 was superseded by the public-permissive/secret-strict alternative in20, agreed in21 and explicitly implemented in22. Comment25 shortens the release wording from24. Historical RFC/RNP support and contributor test statements are attributed, not independently checked current standards or crypto results.",
        "The full review timeline, five actual submitted inline rows and two summary edit histories were reconciled. Review requests a short rationale and a no-keys warning. The author corrects the caller concern: OpenPGPTestUtils was changed; test_secretKeys does not pass the removed parameters. A proposed comment deletion becomes clarification. The earlier all-permissive WIP title does not describe the landed secret-key policy; Try syntax added and removed in summary history does not establish a test pass.",
        "The retained fixed-source checks cover full 0x fingerprint filtering, public acceptance updates, temporary collected-key inspection and secret-key storage tests. Existing native cleanup and nullable-result limits stay scoped: merge cleanup uses finally, but that does not make every import throw path safe. keyRing guards !res and later dereferences res.errorMsg; this is a static concern without a demonstrated reachable failure. Secret import writes importedKeysObj.keys and its checked wizard consumer uses keys; the public wrapper uses value.",
        "The inspected secret-key tests exercise wrong-password failure followed by successful import and protected-versus-unprotected storage counts, with xpcshell registration. They do not establish malformed permissive public-key behavior, exception cleanup, encryption usability or cryptographic correctness. No runtime import, build, lint or test execution ran."
      ],
